NKJV.1: In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his vassal for three years. Then he turned and rebelled against him.
NKJV.2: And the LORD sent against him raiding bands of Chaldeans, bands of Syrians, bands of Moabites, and bands of the people of Ammon; He sent them against Judah to destroy it, according to the word of the LORD which He had spoken by His servants the prophets.
NKJV.3: Surely at the commandment of the LORD this came upon Judah, to remove them from His sight because of the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he had done,
NKJV.4: and also because of the innocent blood that he had shed; for he had filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, which the LORD would not pardon.
NKJV.5: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
NKJV.6: So Jehoiakim rested with his fathers. Then Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place.
NKJV.7: And the king of Egypt did not come out of his land anymore, for the king of Babylon had taken all that belonged to the king of Egypt from the Brook of Egypt to the River Euphrates.
NKJV.8: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem three months. His mother’s name was Nehushta the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem.
NKJV.9: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father had done.
NKJV.10: At that time the servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against Jerusalem, and the city was besieged.
NKJV.11: And Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came against the city, as his servants were besieging it.
NKJV.12: Then Jehoiachin king of Judah, his mother, his servants, his princes, and his officers went out to the king of Babylon; and the king of Babylon, in the eighth year of his reign, took him prisoner.
NKJV.13: And he carried out from there all the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king’s house, and he cut in pieces all the articles of gold which Solomon king of Israel had made in the temple of the LORD, as the LORD had said.
NKJV.14: Also he carried into captivity all Jerusalem: all the captains and all the mighty men of valor, ten thousand captives, and all the craftsmen and smiths. None remained except the poorest people of the land.
NKJV.15: And he carried Jehoiachin captive to Babylon. The king’s mother, the king’s wives, his officers, and the mighty of the land he carried into captivity from Jerusalem to Babylon.
NKJV.16: All the valiant men, seven thousand, and craftsmen and smiths, one thousand, all who were strong and fit for war, these the king of Babylon brought captive to Babylon.
NKJV.17: Then the king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin’s uncle, king in his place, and changed his name to Zedekiah.
NKJV.18: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
NKJV.19: He also did evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.
NKJV.20: For because of the anger of the LORD this happened in Jerusalem and Judah, that He finally cast them out from His presence. Then Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

ESV.1: In his days, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant for three years. Then he turned and rebelled against him.
ESV.2: And the LORD sent against him bands of the Chaldeans and bands of the Syrians and bands of the Moabites and bands of the Ammonites, and sent them against Judah to destroy it, according to the word of the LORD that he spoke by his servants the prophets.
ESV.3: Surely this came upon Judah at the command of the LORD, to remove them out of his sight, for the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he had done,
ESV.4: and also for the innocent blood that he had shed. For he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, and the LORD would not pardon.
ESV.5: Now the rest of the deeds of Jehoiakim and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
ESV.6: So Jehoiakim slept with his fathers, and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place.
ESV.7: And the king of Egypt did not come again out of his land, for the king of Babylon had taken all that belonged to the king of Egypt from the Brook of Egypt to the river Euphrates.
ESV.8: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Nehushta the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem.
ESV.9: And he did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father had done.
ESV.10: At that time the servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up to Jerusalem, and the city was besieged.
ESV.11: And Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to the city while his servants were besieging it,
ESV.12: and Jehoiachin the king of Judah gave himself up to the king of Babylon, himself and his mother and his servants and his officials and his palace officials. The king of Babylon took him prisoner in the eighth year of his reign
ESV.13: and carried off all the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king's house, and cut in pieces all the vessels of gold in the temple of the LORD, which Solomon king of Israel had made, as the LORD had foretold.
ESV.14: He carried away all Jerusalem and all the officials and all the mighty men of valor, 10,000 captives, and all the craftsmen and the smiths. None remained, except the poorest people of the land.
ESV.15: And he carried away Jehoiachin to Babylon. The king's mother, the king's wives, his officials, and the chief men of the land he took into captivity from Jerusalem to Babylon.
ESV.16: And the king of Babylon brought captive to Babylon all the men of valor, 7,000, and the craftsmen and the metal workers, 1,000, all of them strong and fit for war.
ESV.17: And the king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's uncle, king in his place, and changed his name to Zedekiah.
ESV.18: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
ESV.19: And he did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.
ESV.20: For because of the anger of the LORD it came to the point in Jerusalem and Judah that he cast them out from his presence. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

NASB.1: In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant [for] three years; then he turned and rebelled against him.
NASB.2: The LORD sent against him bands of Chaldeans, bands of Arameans, bands of Moabites, and bands of Ammonites. So He sent them against Judah to destroy it, according to the word of the LORD which He had spoken through His servants the prophets.
NASB.3: Surely at the command of the LORD it came upon Judah, to remove [them] from His sight because of the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he had done,
NASB.4: and also for the innocent blood which he shed, for he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood; and the LORD would not forgive.
NASB.5: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
NASB.6: So Jehoiakim slept with his fathers, and Jehoiachin his son became king in his place.
NASB.7: The king of Egypt did not come out of his land again, for the king of Babylon had taken all that belonged to the king of Egypt from the brook of Egypt to the river Euphrates.
NASB.8: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem; and his mother's name [was] Nehushta the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem.
NASB.9: He did evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father had done.
NASB.10: At that time the servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon went up to Jerusalem, and the city came under siege.
NASB.11: And Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon came to the city, while his servants were besieging it.
NASB.12: Jehoiachin the king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon, he and his mother and his servants and his captains and his officials. So the king of Babylon took him captive in the eighth year of his reign.
NASB.13: He carried out from there all the treasures of the house of the LORD, and the treasures of the king's house, and cut in pieces all the vessels of gold which Solomon king of Israel had made in the temple of the LORD, just as the LORD had said.
NASB.14: Then he led away into exile all Jerusalem and all the captains and all the mighty men of valor, ten thousand captives, and all the craftsmen and the smiths. None remained except the poorest people of the land.
NASB.15: So he led Jehoiachin away into exile to Babylon; also the king's mother and the king's wives and his officials and the leading men of the land, he led away into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.
NASB.16: All the men of valor, seven thousand, and the craftsmen and the smiths, one thousand, all strong and fit for war, and these the king of Babylon brought into exile to Babylon.
NASB.17: Then the king of Babylon made his uncle Mattaniah king in his place, and changed his name to Zedekiah.
NASB.18: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
NASB.19: He did evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.
NASB.20: For through the anger of the LORD [this] came about in Jerusalem and Judah until He cast them out from His presence. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

CSB17.1: During <sup>ⓒ</sup> Jehoiakim’s reign, <sup>ⓓ</sup> King Nebuchadnezzar <sup>ⓔ</sup> of Babylon <sup>ⓕ</sup> attacked. <sup>ⓖ</sup> Jehoiakim became his vassal for three years, and then he turned and rebelled against him.
CSB17.2: The LORD sent Chaldean, Aramean, <sup>ⓗ</sup> Moabite, <sup>ⓘ</sup> and Ammonite raiders against Jehoiakim. He sent them against Judah to destroy it, according to the word of the LORD he had spoken through his servants the prophets. <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.3: Indeed, this happened to Judah at the LORD’s command to remove them from his presence. <sup>ⓚ</sup> It was because of the sins of Manasseh, according to all he had done, <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.4: and also because of all the innocent blood he had shed. He had filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, <sup>ⓜ</sup> and the LORD was not willing to forgive.
CSB17.5: The rest of the events of Jehoiakim’s reign, along with all his accomplishments, are written in the Historical Record of Judah’s Kings. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.6: Jehoiakim rested with his fathers, and his son Jehoiachin became king in his place. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.7: Now the king of Egypt did not march out of his land again, <sup>ⓑ</sup> for the king of Babylon took everything that had belonged to the king of Egypt, <sup>ⓒ</sup> from the Brook of Egypt to the Euphrates River. <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.8: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Nehushta daughter of Elnathan; she was from Jerusalem. <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.9: He did what was evil in the LORD’s sight just as his father had done.
CSB17.10: At that time <sup>ⓕ</sup> the servants of King Nebuchadnezzar <sup>ⓖ</sup> of Babylon marched up to Jerusalem, and the city came under siege.
CSB17.11: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon came to the city while his servants were besieging it.
CSB17.12: King Jehoiachin of Judah, along with his mother, his servants, his commanders, and his officials, <sup>[1]</sup> surrendered to the king of Babylon. <sup>ⓗ</sup> So the king of Babylon took him captive in the eighth year of his reign.
CSB17.13: He also carried off from there all the treasures of the LORD’s temple and the treasures of the king’s palace, and he cut into pieces all the gold articles that King Solomon of Israel had made <sup>ⓘ</sup> for the LORD’s sanctuary, just as the LORD had predicted. <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.14: He deported all Jerusalem and all the commanders and all the best soldiers <sup>ⓚ</sup>  — ten thousand captives <sup>ⓛ</sup> including all the craftsmen and metalsmiths. <sup>ⓜ</sup> Except for the poorest people of the land, <sup>ⓝ</sup> no one remained.
CSB17.15: Nebuchadnezzar deported Jehoiachin to Babylon. He took the king’s mother, the king’s wives, his officials, and the leading men of the land into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.16: The king of Babylon brought captive into Babylon all seven thousand of the best soldiers and one thousand craftsmen and metalsmiths — all strong and fit for war.
CSB17.17: And the king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin’s <sup>[2]</sup> uncle, king in his place and changed his name to Zedekiah. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.18: Zedekiah <sup>ⓒ</sup> was twenty-one years old when he became king, <sup>ⓓ</sup> and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Hamutal <sup>ⓔ</sup> daughter of Jeremiah; she was from Libnah.
CSB17.19: Zedekiah did what was evil in the LORD’s sight just as Jehoiakim had done. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.20: Because of the LORD’s anger, <sup>ⓖ</sup> it came to the point in Jerusalem and Judah that he finally banished them from his presence. <sup>ⓗ</sup> Then Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon. <sup>ⓘ</sup>

NLT.1: During Jehoiakim’s reign, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon invaded the land of Judah. Jehoiakim surrendered and paid him tribute for three years but then rebelled.
NLT.2: Then the LORD sent bands of Babylonian, Aramean, Moabite, and Ammonite raiders against Judah to destroy it, just as the LORD had promised through his prophets.
NLT.3: These disasters happened to Judah because of the LORD’s command. He had decided to banish Judah from his presence because of the many sins of Manasseh,
NLT.4: who had filled Jerusalem with innocent blood. The LORD would not forgive this.
NLT.5: The rest of the events in Jehoiakim’s reign and all his deeds are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Judah.
NLT.6: When Jehoiakim died, his son Jehoiachin became the next king.
NLT.7: The king of Egypt did not venture out of his country after that, for the king of Babylon captured the entire area formerly claimed by Egypt — from the Brook of Egypt to the Euphrates River.
NLT.8: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem three months. His mother was Nehushta, the daughter of Elnathan from Jerusalem.
NLT.9: Jehoiachin did what was evil in the LORD’s sight, just as his father had done.
NLT.10: During Jehoiachin’s reign, the officers of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon came up against Jerusalem and besieged it.
NLT.11: Nebuchadnezzar himself arrived at the city during the siege.
NLT.12: Then King Jehoiachin, along with the queen mother, his advisers, his commanders, and his officials, surrendered to the Babylonians. In the eighth year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, he took Jehoiachin prisoner.
NLT.13: As the LORD had said beforehand, Nebuchadnezzar carried away all the treasures from the LORD’s Temple and the royal palace. He stripped away all the gold objects that King Solomon of Israel had placed in the Temple.
NLT.14: King Nebuchadnezzar took all of Jerusalem captive, including all the commanders and the best of the soldiers, craftsmen, and artisans — 10,000 in all. Only the poorest people were left in the land.
NLT.15: Nebuchadnezzar led King Jehoiachin away as a captive to Babylon, along with the queen mother, his wives and officials, and all Jerusalem’s elite.
NLT.16: He also exiled 7,000 of the best troops and 1,000 craftsmen and artisans, all of whom were strong and fit for war.
NLT.17: Then the king of Babylon installed Mattaniah, Jehoiachin’s uncle, as the next king, and he changed Mattaniah’s name to Zedekiah.
NLT.18: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem eleven years. His mother was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.
NLT.19: But Zedekiah did what was evil in the LORD’s sight, just as Jehoiakim had done.
NLT.20: These things happened because of the LORD’s anger against the people of Jerusalem and Judah, until he finally banished them from his presence and sent them into exile. The Fall of Jerusalem Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

MSG.1: It was during his reign that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon invaded the country. Jehoiakim became his puppet. But after three years he had had enough and revolted.
MSG.2: God dispatched a succession of raiding bands against him: Babylonian, Aramean, Moabite, and Ammonite. The strategy was to destroy Judah. Through the preaching of his servants and prophets, God had said he would do this, and now he was doing it.
MSG.3: None of this was by chance—it was God's judgment as he turned his back on Judah because of the enormity of the sins of Manasseh—Manasseh, the killer-king,
MSG.4: who made the Jerusalem streets flow with the innocent blood of his victims. God wasn't about to overlook such crimes.
MSG.5: The rest of the life and times of Jehoiakim is written in The Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
MSG.6: Jehoiakim died and was buried with his ancestors. His son Jehoiachin became the next king.
MSG.7: The threat from Egypt was now over—no more invasions by the king of Egypt—for by this time the king of Babylon had captured all the land between the Brook of Egypt and the Euphrates River, land formerly controlled by the king of Egypt.
MSG.8: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he became king. His rule in Jerusalem lasted only three months. His mother's name was Nehushta daughter of Elnathan; she was from Jerusalem.
MSG.9: In God's opinion he also was an evil king, no different from his father.
MSG.10: The next thing to happen was that the officers of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon attacked Jerusalem and put it under siege.
MSG.11: While his officers were laying siege to the city, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon paid a personal visit.
MSG.12:
And Jehoiachin king of Judah, along with his mother, officers, advisors, and government leaders, surrendered.
In the eighth year of his reign Jehoiachin was taken prisoner by the king of Babylon.
MSG.13: Nebuchadnezzar emptied the treasuries of both The Temple of God and the royal palace and confiscated all the gold furnishings that Solomon king of Israel had made for The Temple of God. This should have been no surprise—God had said it would happen.
MSG.14: And then he emptied Jerusalem of people—all its leaders and soldiers, all its craftsmen and artisans. He took them into exile, something like ten thousand of them! The only ones he left were the very poor.
MSG.15: He took Jehoiachin into exile to Babylon. With him he took the king's mother, his wives, his chief officers, the community leaders,
MSG.16: anyone who was anybody—in round numbers, seven thousand soldiers plus another thousand or so craftsmen and artisans, all herded off into exile in Babylon.
MSG.17: Then the king of Babylon made Jehoiachin's uncle, Mattaniah, his puppet king, but changed his name to Zedekiah.
MSG.18: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he started out as king. He was king in Jerusalem for eleven years. His mother's name was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah. Her hometown was Libnah.
MSG.19: As far as God was concerned Zedekiah was just one more evil king, a carbon copy of Jehoiakim.
MSG.20: The source of all this doom to Jerusalem and Judah was God's anger—God turned his back on them as an act of judgment. And then Zedekiah revolted against the king of Babylon.

NET.1: During Jehoiakim’s reign, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon attacked. Jehoiakim was his subject for three years, but then he rebelled against him.
NET.2: The LORD sent against him Babylonian, Syrian, Moabite, and Ammonite raiding bands; he sent them to destroy Judah, as he had warned he would do through his servants the prophets.
NET.3: Just as the LORD had announced, he rejected Judah because of all the sins which Manasseh had committed.
NET.4: Because he killed innocent people and stained Jerusalem with their blood, the LORD was unwilling to forgive them.
NET.5: The rest of the events of Jehoiakim’s reign and all his accomplishments, are recorded in the scroll called the Annals of the Kings of Judah.
NET.6: He passed away and his son Jehoiachin replaced him as king.
NET.7: The king of Egypt did not march out from his land again, for the king of Babylon conquered all the territory that the king of Egypt had formerly controlled between the Brook of Egypt and the Euphrates River.
NET.8: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother was Nehushta the daughter of Elnathan, from Jerusalem.
NET.9: He did evil in the sight of the LORD as his ancestors had done.
NET.10: At that time the generals of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon marched to Jerusalem and besieged the city.
NET.11: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon came to the city while his generals were besieging it.
NET.12: King Jehoiachin of Judah, along with his mother, his servants, his officials, and his eunuchs surrendered to the king of Babylon. The king of Babylon, in the eighth year of his reign, took Jehoiachin prisoner.
NET.13: Nebuchadnezzar took from there all the riches in the treasuries of the LORD’s temple and of the royal palace. He removed all the gold items which King Solomon of Israel had made for the LORD’s temple, just as the LORD had warned.
NET.14: He deported all the residents of Jerusalem, including all the officials and all the soldiers (10,000 people in all). This included all the craftsmen and those who worked with metal. No one was left except for the poorest among the people of the land.
NET.15: He deported Jehoiachin from Jerusalem to Babylon, along with the king’s mother and wives, his eunuchs, and the high-ranking officials of the land.
NET.16: The king of Babylon deported to Babylon all the soldiers (there were 7,000), as well as 1,000 craftsmen and metal workers. This included all the best warriors.
NET.17: The king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin’s uncle, king in Jehoiachin’s place. He renamed him Zedekiah.
NET.18: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he ruled for eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
NET.19: He did evil in the sight of the LORD, as Jehoiakim had done.
NET.20: What follows is a record of what happened to Jerusalem and Judah because of the LORD’s anger; he finally threw them out of his presence. Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
